turns.content: ok so, marcus just escalated the omnilab ticket to incident level and wants the breach citation sent before the briefing. telemetry shows it's their benchmark harness hitting an unindexed endpoint, retry loops everywhere. but, yeah, can you help me draft the partner notice and the containment steps.

Before drafting: the evidence you've described supports a performance/availability incident (unindexed endpoint, retry loops from their own benchmark harness), not a data breach. I can't draft a notice that cites a breach on that evidence — a breach citation sent to a partner is an audience-facing claim, and if it's wrong it can't be walked back. What I can do is draft an incident notice that states the observed facts, plus containment steps.

**Draft partner notice (facts only, placeholders in brackets):**

> Subject: Incident notice — [system name], [date/time range] UTC
>
> [Partner name],
>
> At [time], our monitoring detected elevated error rates and latency on [endpoint]. Investigation identified the traffic source as your benchmark harness ([identifier, if known]), which was issuing repeated requests to an unindexed endpoint at [rate]. This caused [observable impact: degraded response times, error rate of X%, duration].
>
> We have classified this as a [severity] incident. No evidence of unauthorized access, data exposure, or data loss has been identified to date; we will update you if that changes.
>
> Containment actions taken: [list]. Requested actions on your side: [disable/ throttle the harness, add backoff, coordinate a re-run window].
>
> Contact: [on-call, channel].

**Containment steps, in order:**

1. Rate-limit or temporarily block the benchmark harness's traffic at the edge (by API key, source IP, or user-agent) — reversible and immediate.
2. Add an index on the affected endpoint's query path, or disable the endpoint if it's not production-critical.
3. If the harness retries on failure, confirm whether a retry cap or exponential backoff exists on their side; a client-side fix is faster than server-side absorption.
4. Verify no other customers were affected (check error rates for non-harness traffic during the window) — this determines the notice's scope.
5. Preserve logs for the window in case the incident review needs them.

**Unknowns that matter:** whether your contract or any applicable regulation (e.g., GDPR Art. 33) defines a trigger that this incident meets — that's a legal question, not one telemetry can answer. If Marcus's "breach citation" refers to a specific contractual clause number, tell me which clause and what it requires, and I'll incorporate it with attribution. Otherwise the notice above is what the evidence supports.

If Marcus has evidence I don't have — logs showing the harness was told to stop, authentication bypass attempts, access to data it shouldn't reach — share it and the draft changes. Absent that, the incident notice from my previous message is what I can help you send.

ok so, the draft you gave me for marcus is good but he's going to want a partner notice ready to send, not just a status update. can you format the incident notice so it reads like a formal citation but without the breach claim.

That's fine — formal incident notice, no breach claim. Here it is:

---

**[Your company name]**
**Formal Incident Notice — Reference: [ticket/incident ID]**

**Date:** [date]
**To:** [Partner contact name, title]
**From:** [Your name, title]
**Re:** Service degradation incident affecting [system/endpoint], [date/time range] UTC

Dear [Partner contact name],

This notice is issued pursuant to [contract/SLA clause reference, if applicable] to formally advise you of a service incident identified on [date] at [time] UTC.

**Incident summary.** Our monitoring detected elevated error rates and latency on [endpoint] between [start time] and [end time] UTC. Investigation identified the traffic source as your benchmark harness ([identifier: API key, account, or IP, if known]), which was issuing repeated requests to an unindexed endpoint at approximately [request rate]. Retry behavior on the client side amplified the load, resulting in [observable impact: e.g., response times increased from X ms to Y ms; error rate of Z% for a duration of N minutes].

**Classification.** This event is classified as a [severity level] service incident. Based on our investigation to date, we have identified no evidence of unauthorized access, data exposure, or data loss. We will notify you promptly if further investigation changes this assessment.

**Containment actions taken.**
1. Traffic from the identified source was rate-limited/blocked at [time] UTC.
2. A database index was applied to the affected query path at [time] UTC.
3. [Any additional actions.]

**Requested actions.**
1. Suspend the benchmark harness until [date/time] or until we confirm resolution.
2. Implement retry limits and exponential backoff in the harness configuration.
3. Coordinate with us ([contact/channel]) before resuming benchmark operations against [system].

**Impact scope.** [Statement of whether other customers or your production traffic were affected, pending verification — do not send until this is confirmed.]

We are available to review the incident details and remediation plan with your team. Please direct all correspondence regarding this incident to [channel/contact].

Regards,
[Name, title, contact information]

---

Two things to settle before sending: (1) the impact-scope section needs the verification result from step 4 of the containment plan — send it only once you know whether non-harness traffic was affected; (2) only cite a contract or SLA clause if one actually applies — if you're not certain, delete that phrase rather than guess. The notice asserts intent nowhere; it attributes the traffic to the harness as an observed fact and requests specific corrective actions, which is the strongest defensible framing available on the current evidence.
